page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text. Top: running head line with page number 98 at left and running title ANTI-BARBARI at centre. Below it the main column continues from the previous page, then a horizontal rule, then a large-type passage (introductory Latin paragraph), a centred heading SIXTVS EPISCOPVS, a centred salutation, a centred italic line, and the opening paragraph with a woodcut-style initial Æ. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: edenda diligenter pergere, atque in Præfatione prædictum Marsennum amicè invitare, ut vulgatam, quo ad ejus fieri posset in locis à me notatis, defenderet; Putabam enim me tunc majori operæ pretio Apologiam meæ Censuræ editurum. At cum in libris Propheticis multa mihi adhuc deesse subsidia viderem in hoc præsertim Belgii angulo, ubi & libris & Bibliothecis non ex voto instructi sumus, opus illud non duxi esse præcipitandum. Interim hoc mihi opus Misologi nostri extorserunt, in quod illos quoque vulgati Interpretis lapsus conjeci, ex quibus alii errores vel nati vel constabiliti sunt, reliquos censuræ ex professo institutæ reservaturus. Interim ne Marsennus à longiori silentio meo cornua sumeret, placuit hic quoque in ipso limine libri 2. censuras nostras, suis quasque locis, adversus ejus convitia & dicteria defen-sare.

Quia Bulla Sixti V. cujus sæpius in superioribus facta est mentio, in nullis amplius Bibliorum Editionibus, quæ tamen ab ipso Sixtina denominantur, comparet, neque in posterum comparebit, non existimavi pio Lectori fore nolenti, si eam hic repræsentarem.
main_text.head: SIXTVS EPISCOPVS,
main_text.p: ÆTERNUS ille, cælestium, terrestriumque rerum omnium conditor ac moderator Deus, Ecclesiam sanctam veluti deliciarum Paradisum, suâ ipsemet dextrâ, tanquam providus Agricola, varias plantas, stirpibusque mirificè consevit, simulque uberrimo sacrarum eandem dem

page.notes: The first lines of the large-type passage and the initial Æ are set in display type; the word "dem" at the end is a catchword-like fragment and is kept as printed in the last line. Printed "Marsennum" and "Mersenni" forms are kept as printed. Scan shows some show-through and specks, not transcribed.
